title: ～ておく — “do ～ in advance”
summary: Attach おく to the te-form to do something ahead of time for later. It also means leaving something as it is.

patterns.gloss: Verb te-form + おく (買っておく)

body.p: Use it for preparing so you are not in trouble later: 旅行の前に切符を買っておく. Past: ～ておいた.
In casual speech ～ておく contracts to ～とく (買っとく). It can also mean leaving a state as is, as in 窓を開けておく.

examples.ja: 旅行（りょこう）の前（まえ）に切符（きっぷ）を買（か）っておきます。
examples.romaji: Ryokō no mae ni kippu o katte okimasu.
examples.tr: I'll buy the tickets in advance before the trip.

examples.ja: 客（きゃく）が来（く）る前（まえ）に部屋（へや）を掃除（そうじ）しておきます。
examples.romaji: Kyaku ga kuru mae ni heya o sōji shite okimasu.
examples.tr: I'll clean the room in advance before the guests come.

examples.ja: 会議（かいぎ）の資料（しりょう）を先（さき）にコピーしておいた。
examples.romaji: Kaigi no shiryō o saki ni kopī shite oita.
examples.tr: I made copies of the meeting materials beforehand.

pitfalls: Do not confuse it with state ている.
It is for deliberate preparation, so use it with volitional verbs.
